t: Component Boundary Designer - Signature build-tool concept
title: Component Boundary Designer - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Defines the responsibilities and interfaces of components.
description:
The Signature Component Boundary Designer exists to defines the responsibilities and interfaces of components. It is one of the fundamental capabilities in the AI build-tool catalog: the set of tools, engines and disciplines an AI needs to design, engineer, generate, test and deliver things on demand. Where public tools each solve a slice of the problem, the Signature line defines the whole capability as a coherent framework with contracts between its parts.

Consider what happens without a disciplined Component Boundary Designer. Component Boundary Designer work degrades into folklore - tricks that work on one machine, steps remembered differently by every practitioner, failures nobody can reproduce. The Signature framework answers with determinism: declared inputs, explicit transformations, verified outputs, and an audit trail that explains every result. The pillars below are the machinery that makes that promise concrete.

This is a Signature-concept database: the framework it describes is the Signature line's own design, labeled as such throughout. The techniques and standards records cite real public knowledge; the pillars and drills are the Signature system's original construction. All of it ships with runnable demos, because in the Signature line a tool proves itself by running.

t: Signature Cartographer - Component Boundary Designer framework pillar
title: Signature Cartographer - Component Boundary Designer framework pillar
definition: The Cartographer component of the Signature Component Boundary Designer framework, owning cartographer. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature Component Boundary Designer framework, the Cartographer owns the framework's cartographer responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Cartographer's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Cartographer from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Defines the responsibilities and interfaces of components.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Walk through it concretely. A Software architecture and system design build needs Component Boundary Designer, so the framework invokes the Cartographer on the the framework's cartographer responsibilities portion of the work. The demo program attached to this record executes the pillar's essential algorithm on sample data - run it with node and watch each step print its reasoning. Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Component Boundary Designer. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Contractor - Component Boundary Designer framework pillar
title: Signature Contractor - Component Boundary Designer framework pillar
definition: The Contractor component of the Signature Component Boundary Designer framework, owning contractor. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Component Boundary Designer framework decomposes the capability (Defines the responsibilities and interfaces of components.) into seven pillars, and the Contractor is the one that owns the framework's contractor responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Component Boundary Designer result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Contractor's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Contractor's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Component Boundary Designer. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Stratifier - Component Boundary Designer framework pillar
title: Signature Stratifier - Component Boundary Designer framework pillar
definition: The Stratifier component of the Signature Component Boundary Designer framework, owning stratifier. Signature concept.
description:
The Stratifier is a load-bearing component of the Signature Component Boundary Designer framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's stratifier responsibilities belongs to the Stratifier, and the Stratifier answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Stratifier can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Stratifier works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Component Boundary Designer charter (defines the responsibilities and interfaces of components.). The Stratifier reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for an small architecture job that needs Component Boundary Designer. The Stratifier takes the request's stratifier responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Stratifier's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Component Boundary Designer. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

Drill (FOUNDATION): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Component Boundary Designer from a one-paragraph brief
